endorsements.quote: In addition to the considerations outlined above, we recommend the establishment of a departmental review (or assessment) board specifically for the procurement of AI solutions.

Despite this, radiologists should still evaluate potential financial benefits and roughly estimate the ROI, while also considering other key factors, such as clinical relevance, performance, implementation, and simplicity.
Implementation and integration A critical, yet often overlooked, aspect of AI products is the ease of integration into the existing workflow of a radiology department.

We suggest that a successful AI solution must be fully integrated with PACS, featuring a user-friendly interface that can be used with minimal mouse clicks, or even without any clicks in a fully automated fashion for high-volume examinations.

Such a solution should immediately distinguish pathological cases from normal ones with binary classification, ideally identify priority cases with acute findings, and highlight them on the radiologist\u2019s worklist for triage.
Evidence of external validation: Seek validation from external independent bodies, studies, or reference centers.

Vendor data usage policies: Review the AI vendor\u2019s policies regarding the use of hospital data, particularly clauses related to data usage for product improvement or other purposes, to ensure alignment with the hospital\u2019s data privacy policies.

Adherence to data protection laws: Confirm that the AI solution adheres to health data protection standards relevant to the region, such as HIPAA in the United States or GDPR in Europe, and any national standards, such as T\u00fcrkiye\u2019s KVKK.

Data security measures: Evaluate the AI system\u2019s data security measures, including encryption protocols and access controls, to ensure patient data are protected, particularly if cloud-based solutions are used.
Pilot testing: Consider conducting a pilot test using the AI solution within the department to observe its real-time performance and impact.
Compliance with international standards: Verify that the AI system complies with international regulatory standards, such as the FDA in the United States and the European Union\u2019s CE marking.

Trial integration and IT assessment: Conduct a trial integration of the AI solution with the assistance of IT professionals to identify potential compliance or technical issues before full implementation.

unlisted_practices: Compare AI purchasing models, such as annual licenses versus per-use fees, to identify the most cost-effective option.
Assess vendor implementation support, including whether implementation is outsourced to a third party.
Verify AI tool compatibility with existing PACS, imaging modalities, and hardware before purchase.
Check whether the AI solution can store data locally where data residency laws require it.
Assess the availability of insurance reimbursement for the AI solution.

screen.reason: This is a guidance/framework paper offering practical recommendations and key factors for radiology departments to consider when selecting and deploying AI solutions.
